dct_title_s: Venezuela - M 7.5 Earthquake - Building Damage Assessment ( fAIr )
dct_description_sm: This dataset contains AI-generated data exported from fAIr (fair.hotosm.org) by HOTOSM in response to the magnitude 7.5 earthquake that struck Venezuela in June 2026. GLIDE: EQ-2026-000093-VEN. On Wednesday, 24 June 2026, Venezuela was struck by two of the most powerful earthquakes the country has seen in over a century. The back-to-back tremors caused widespread damage, particularly in La Guaira and the capital, Caracas, and along the northern coast. Building damage assessment data is available for La Guaira. Building-level damage assessment produced by the damage assessment AI model developed by HOTOSM on the fAIr platform. Each point flags an area where possibly damaged buildings are located, with a predicted damage level and a confidence score. Categories: - 🔴 Red - destroyed - 🟠 Orange - major damage - 🟡 Yellow - minor damage Data - Post-disaster imagery: Vantor WorldView-3, 0.34 m, acquired 2026-06-26, via OpenAerialMap ([TMS](https://tiles.openaerialmap.org/6a3f2d9090cf21f32ffb619c/0/6a3f2d9090cf21f32ffb619d/{z}/{x}/{y})). - Building footprints: fAIr predictions run on the post-event imagery at its native 0.34 m resolution. How to use - Treat every point as a candidate for human review, not a confirmed result. A validation project is being set up. - Obvious false positives have been removed; anything with a trace of damage is kept.
